# LogicGates.org

> Free digital logic tools and reference, running entirely in the browser. Truth tables, Karnaugh maps, boolean algebra, sum of products, NAND and NOR conversion, circuit diagrams, expression trees, binary and Gray code; propositional logic with truth tables for logic statements, step-by-step equivalence proofs, rules of inference, conditional statements and tautologies; Venn diagrams and set notation; hex, binary and IEEE 754 converters and binary and hex calculators that show their working; a binary translator, an ASCII table and Base64; plus a full reference for the seven logic gates, De Morgan's laws, worked simplification examples, the Quine-McCluskey method, the SR latch, flip-flops, finite state machines, the seven-segment decoder, a glossary, counters, shift registers, the ripple carry adder, two's complement and the laws of boolean algebra, practice questions, printable worksheets, and a logic gate simulator. No account, no install, no tracking.

Every truth table, identity, proof step and gate count on the site is generated by the site's own engines and checked by a property-based test suite, so the published content cannot drift from the maths. Open source under Apache 2.0. The simulator (originally released as Logic Nodes) is a hand-written TypeScript application rendering on an HTML5 canvas.

## Pages

- [Home](https://logicgates.org/): the hub, with every tool and reference page, and an FAQ
- [Tools index](https://logicgates.org/tools): every calculator and generator in one place
- [Simulator](https://logicgates.org/simulator): the Logic Nodes editor itself, opens with an example circuit
- [Learn digital logic](https://logicgates.org/learn): a free interactive course in eight stages and about 35 lessons, from bits and gates through boolean algebra, Karnaugh maps, adders, latches and flip-flops to counters and state machines; each lesson at /learn/<lesson> explains the idea in plain words, has a live circuit to click, and ends with a generated quiz with hints (progress kept in the browser)
- [Logic gates reference](https://logicgates.org/logic-gates): what a logic gate is, the seven types, universal gates, a short history and an FAQ, each gate with its own page (/logic-gates/and, /or, /not, /xor, /nand, /nor, /xnor)
- [Logic gate symbols](https://logicgates.org/logic-gate-symbols): ANSI distinctive shapes and IEC rectangles side by side
- [De Morgan's laws](https://logicgates.org/de-morgans-laws): both laws stated, proved by generated truth tables, with worked examples, the n-variable form, bubble pushing on schematics and the common mistake
- [SR latch](https://logicgates.org/sr-latch): the NOR and NAND latches, the gated SR latch and the D latch, each with a generated truth table and step diagram, and how a latch differs from a flip-flop
- [Flip-flops](https://logicgates.org/flip-flops): SR, D, JK and T, each with characteristic and excitation tables, a generated timing diagram and a clockable demo (/flip-flops/sr, /d, /jk, /t)
- [Counters](https://logicgates.org/counters): how binary counters work, ripple vs synchronous, decade and up/down, with generated count tables and timing diagrams
- [Shift registers](https://logicgates.org/shift-registers): SISO, SIPO, PISO and PIPO, plus ring and Johnson counters, with generated timing diagrams
- [Circuit diagram generator](https://logicgates.org/logic-circuit-generator): draws an expression as a gate diagram with live signal colours
- [Practice](https://logicgates.org/practice): endless generated questions on gates, truth tables and expressions, marked instantly, filterable by topic
- [Worksheet generator](https://logicgates.org/worksheet): a printable worksheet with an optional answer key, rebuilt from the sheet number in the link, so a class can be given the same questions without any account or storage
- [Common circuits](https://logicgates.org/common-circuits): half and full adders and subtractors, multiplexer, demultiplexer, 2-to-4 and 3-to-8 decoders, encoder, 1-bit and 2-bit comparators, parity and majority, each with expressions and a generated truth table, and each with its own page (/common-circuits/half-adder, /full-adder, /half-subtractor, /full-subtractor, /multiplexer, /demultiplexer, /decoder, /decoder-3-to-8, /encoder, /comparator, /comparator-2-bit, /parity, /majority)
- [Ripple carry adder](https://logicgates.org/ripple-carry-adder): the full adder cell, a 4-bit adder with a live circuit diagram and a column by column trace, why the carry chain is slow, the carry lookahead equations and their cost, and subtraction with the same adder
- [Two's complement](https://logicgates.org/twos-complement): every 4-bit pattern read as unsigned, sign-magnitude, one's and two's complement, negation by invert and add 1 with a live example, worked signed addition and subtraction, the overflow rule, ranges and sign extension
- [Combinational vs sequential logic](https://logicgates.org/combinational-vs-sequential): what changes once a circuit has feedback, and why a clock appears
- [Finite state machines](https://logicgates.org/finite-state-machines): what a state machine is, Moore vs Mealy, the design procedure, and a 101 sequence detector worked from state diagram to K-map equations, circuit and timing, in both forms
- [Seven-segment decoder](https://logicgates.org/seven-segment-decoder): the BCD to seven-segment truth table, a Karnaugh-map derived expression per segment with codes 10 to 15 as don't cares, a live display and the circuit
- [Boolean algebra examples](https://logicgates.org/boolean-algebra-examples): twelve expressions simplified step by step with the law named on every line, each verified to reach the minimal form
- [Glossary](https://logicgates.org/glossary): every digital logic term on the site defined in one paragraph, linked to its page
- [Quine-McCluskey method](https://logicgates.org/quine-mccluskey): the tabular minimisation worked step by step on any function typed as minterms and don't cares: grouping by 1s, merging passes, the prime implicant chart, essential primes and Petrick's method
- [Karnaugh map solver](https://logicgates.org/karnaugh-map-solver): draws the K-map with the groups highlighted, 2 to 6 variables, supports don't cares (click a square to cycle 0/1/X, or list the row numbers)
- [Sum of products calculator](https://logicgates.org/sum-of-products-calculator): minterms, maxterms, canonical and minimal SOP and POS
- [NAND and NOR converter](https://logicgates.org/nand-nor-converter): rewrites an expression using only NAND or only NOR gates, with gate counts
- [Binary converter](https://logicgates.org/binary-converter): decimal, binary, hex and octal at a fixed bit width, with two's complement, BCD and Gray code, and a clickable register
- [Gray code converter](https://logicgates.org/gray-code-converter): binary to Gray and back, with the full sequence for 2 to 8 bits
- [Boolean algebra laws](https://logicgates.org/boolean-algebra-laws): 28 identities, each proved with a generated truth table
- [Truth table generator](https://logicgates.org/truth-table-generator): turns a typed boolean expression into its truth table, plus the truth tables of the seven basic gates
- [Truth tables for logic statements](https://logicgates.org/propositional-logic-truth-table): truth tables for propositional logic (¬, ∧, ∨, →, ↔) with a column per step, and checks for tautologies, equivalence and argument validity
- [Boolean algebra calculator](https://logicgates.org/boolean-algebra-calculator): simplifies an expression to a minimal sum of products (Quine-McCluskey), shows the working one named law at a time, checks whether two expressions are equivalent, and lists the laws
- [Logical equivalence calculator](https://logicgates.org/logical-equivalence-calculator): proves two logic statements equivalent step by step, one named law per line (conditional, biconditional, De Morgan's, distributive and the rest), or gives a counterexample row when they are not; also simplifies one statement or shows it is a tautology
- [Expression tree generator](https://logicgates.org/expression-tree): draws the parse tree of a logic or boolean expression and evaluates every node from the leaves up, for any row of the truth table
- [Venn diagram generator](https://logicgates.org/venn-diagram-generator): shades the regions of a set expression over one to three sets (∪ ∩ complement, difference, symmetric difference), or gives the shortest expression for regions you click, with each region's truth table row
- [Set notation](https://logicgates.org/set-notation): set symbols with how to read them and computed examples, roster and set-builder notation, and the laws of set algebra, each checked
- [Propositional logic](https://logicgates.org/logic): the connectives (¬ ∧ ∨ ⊕ → ↔) with how to read them, order of operations, and guides to the topics below
- [Conditional statements](https://logicgates.org/logic/conditional-statements): if-then statements, converse, inverse and contrapositive with a generated truth table, the biconditional, necessary and sufficient conditions, "only if" and "unless"
- [Tautology, contradiction and contingency](https://logicgates.org/logic/tautology): definitions, how to check with a truth table, famous tautologies, and why an argument is valid exactly when its conditional form is a tautology
- [Rules of inference](https://logicgates.org/logic/rules-of-inference): modus ponens, modus tollens, syllogisms, addition, simplification, conjunction, resolution and constructive dilemma, each checked valid by truth table, the common fallacies with counterexamples, and a worked proof
- [Logical equivalences](https://logicgates.org/logic/logical-equivalences): the laws of logic, including the conditional and biconditional equivalences, each verified by truth table, with worked proofs by chains of laws
- [Hex to decimal converter](https://logicgates.org/hex-to-decimal): hex to decimal and back, with the place-value sum and repeated division written out
- [Hex to binary converter](https://logicgates.org/hex-to-binary): hex to binary and back nibble by nibble, and octal in groups of three bits
- [Binary calculator](https://logicgates.org/binary-calculator): binary addition, subtraction, multiplication and division with every carry, borrow and partial product shown, plus bitwise operations and fixed widths
- [Hex calculator](https://logicgates.org/hex-calculator): hexadecimal arithmetic with column working, carries at 16, and the hex addition table
- [IEEE 754 converter](https://logicgates.org/ieee-754-converter): decimal to single and double precision floating point bits, with sign, exponent and fraction, the exact value stored, the rounding error, and special values
- [Binary translator](https://logicgates.org/binary-translator): text to binary and binary to text, with each character's code point and UTF-8 bytes
- [ASCII table](https://logicgates.org/ascii-table): all 128 ASCII codes in decimal, hex and binary, with the control characters named and explained
- [Base64 encode and decode](https://logicgates.org/base64): Base64 encoding and decoding (standard and URL-safe), with the bytes regrouped into 6-bit characters step by step
- [Logic symbols to copy and paste](https://logicgates.org/logic-symbols-copy-paste): 64 logic, boolean algebra, set and relation symbols (¬ ∧ ∨ ⊕ → ↔ ∀ ∃ ⊢ ⊨ ∴ ∈ ⊆ ∪ ∅ ℝ and more) with one-click copy, Unicode code points, HTML entities, LaTeX commands (amssymb flagged) and Word Alt+X codes
- [FP16, BF16, FP8 and FP4 converter](https://logicgates.org/fp16-bf16-fp8-converter): decimal to FP16, BF16, FP8 E4M3 and E5M2, FP4 E2M1 and FP32 side by side, with the bits, exact stored value, rounding error, guard/round/sticky rounding, overflow behaviour, a format comparison table, every E4M3 and FP4 code, and MXFP4 block scaling
- [Base 36 converter](https://logicgates.org/base36): converts decimal to base 36 and back, or between any two bases from 2 to 36, for whole numbers of any size, with place values and repeated division shown, plus text as a base 36 number
- [Guess my number](https://logicgates.org/guess-my-number): a binary search game that finds any number from 1 to 100 in 7 yes/no questions, with bit questions that spell 0 to 127 in binary, a liar mode (Ulam's game) where a shortened Hamming(11, 7) code finds the number and names the lie, and a higher/lower mode with an evil adversary that forces the worst case
- [Base32 encode and decode](https://logicgates.org/base32): Base32 encoder and decoder for RFC 4648, base32hex and Crockford alphabets, showing how 5 bytes become 8 characters bit by bit, padding, sizes and 2FA secret keys
- [Base58 encode and decode](https://logicgates.org/base58): Base58 encoder and decoder with repeated division by 58 shown, leading zero bytes as 1s, and a Base58Check checker that splits a Bitcoin address into version, payload and checksum
- [QR code generator](https://logicgates.org/qr-code-generator): a from-scratch QR encoder (numeric, alphanumeric and byte modes, versions 1 to 40, levels L/M/Q/H) that colours every module by role (finder, timing, alignment, format and version information, data and error correction codewords numbered in placement order, remainder bits, quiet zone), scores all eight masks, writes out the bit stream, codewords, Reed-Solomon blocks and interleaving, and downloads SVG or PNG
- [EAN-13 barcode generator](https://logicgates.org/ean-13-barcode-generator): EAN-13, UPC-A and EAN-8 barcodes as SVG or PNG, with the check digit worked out, the L, G and R codes and first-digit parity pattern, guards, quiet zones and all 95 modules; ISBN-10 to ISBN-13 conversion and GS1 prefixes (issuing organisation, not country of origin)
- [Punch card generator and reader](https://logicgates.org/punch-card-generator): punch text onto an 80-column IBM 029 card or a Baudot or ASCII paper tape, or click holes and read the text back, with the zone and digit punches shown
- [Bitwise pattern generator](https://logicgates.org/bitwise-pattern-generator): draw images from expressions in x and y such as x ^ y and x & y, with colour modes, bit planes, the bits behind each pixel and PNG or SVG download
- [Seven-segment and dot-matrix display designer](https://logicgates.org/seven-segment-display-designer): design seven-segment, 5x7 and 8x8 dot-matrix and Nixie displays and export the bytes as C, Arduino or Verilog, with anode and cathode and bit order options
- [Subnet calculator](https://logicgates.org/subnet-calculator): IPv4 network and broadcast address, host range, netmask, wildcard, class and special-use range from any CIDR or mask, with the address AND mask shown bit by bit, an in-subnet check and a /0 to /32 table
- [VLSM calculator](https://logicgates.org/vlsm-calculator): plans IPv4 subnets of different sizes from host counts, largest first and aligned, with masks, host ranges, an address-space bar, free blocks and the shortfall when a plan does not fit, plus equal splits
- [IPv6 expand and compress](https://logicgates.org/ipv6-expand-compress): IPv6 addresses expanded in full and compressed to the RFC 5952 canonical form, with the rule behind each change, all 128 bits, prefix ranges and /64 counts, address types (link-local, unique local, multicast scope, IPv4-mapped, Teredo, NAT64, 6to4) and the EUI-64 identifier from a MAC address
- [Bit manipulation tricks](https://logicgates.org/bit-manipulation-tricks): 22 classic bit hacks (test/set/clear/toggle bit n, x & (x - 1), x & -x, power of two, trailing zeros, Kernighan and SWAR popcount, parity, XOR swap, opposite signs, branchless abs and min/max, average without overflow, modulo a power of two, round up to a power of two, bit reversal, Gray code, sign extension, ASCII case toggle), each traced bit by bit at 8, 16 or 32 bits with why it works, a cheat sheet and verified JavaScript, Python, C and Java gotchas
- [Integer limits](https://logicgates.org/integer-limits): minimum and maximum of every integer type from int8 to uint128 in decimal, hex and binary, their names in C, Java, C#, Rust, Go, Swift, Kotlin, SQL and JavaScript, what each language does on overflow, an overflow playground and a smallest-type lookup, with one page per type at /integer-limits/int32 and so on
- [Struct padding calculator](https://logicgates.org/struct-padding-calculator): C struct and union memory layout with every offset, padding byte, sizeof and alignment on x86-64, Windows, 32-bit x86, ARM and AArch64, #pragma pack, packed and _Alignas, and a reordering that removes padding
- [UUID decoder and generator](https://logicgates.org/uuid-decoder): decodes UUIDs of every version (version, variant, v1/v6/v7 timestamps, clock sequence, node), ULIDs and MongoDB ObjectIds with a labelled bit layout, and generates UUID v4/v7/v1, ULID, ObjectId, NanoID and Discord snowflakes in the browser
- [Snowflake ID decoder](https://logicgates.org/snowflake-id-decoder): decodes Discord and Twitter/X snowflake IDs to their timestamp (UTC, local time and age) with the worker/process/increment or machine/sequence bits, and converts a date to the range of snowflakes for that millisecond
- [File signature checker](https://logicgates.org/file-signature-checker): identify a file's real type from its magic bytes (pick a file, read locally, or paste hex), with a highlighted hex dump, ZIP/MP4 container detection, the CAFEBABE Java vs Mach-O question, extension mismatch check and a signature reference table

## Key facts

- Free and open source (Apache 2.0): https://github.com/semvis123/logic-nodes
- Simulator gates: AND, OR, NOT, XOR, NAND, NOR (AND/OR/NAND/NOR accept any number of inputs; XNOR is an XOR into a NOT), plus interval, delay, counter, button, toggle, constant, splitter, label, microphone, tone, display and output nodes
- Generates truth tables and boolean expressions from circuits, and circuits from truth tables or expressions
- Circuit diagrams and truth tables export as SVG or PNG, in colour or black and white, with ANSI or IEC gate symbols
- Circuits save in the browser (localStorage) with autosave, export and import as JSON files, and copy to the clipboard as JSON
- Built-in examples open from a link: https://logicgates.org/simulator#example:Calculator (also Introduction, 7 Segment-display, Rising edge detector, Falling edge detector)
- Custom nodes let you package circuits into reusable components
- Suited for learning digital logic: boolean algebra, SR latches, half adders, counters
- Built for mouse and keyboard: no pinch to zoom or touch panning, so desktop is the better experience
- Optional boolean expression simplification via Wolfram Alpha requires the user's own App ID
